title: Floating and Sinking
guideExplore: Compare object density to fluid density — watch the object float, sink, or suspend.
guideCork: Cork floats because it is less dense than water.
guideSuspend: Matching densities give neutral buoyancy — the object suspends.
guideRock: A dense rock sinks because it is heavier than the displaced fluid.
conditionsHint: Float when object density < fluid density; sink when denser.
learnMore: Whether an object floats depends on density — how much mass is packed into each cm³ compared to the fluid.
